label: Only air-breathing animals are internally viviparous
claim: No animal is internally viviparous unless it takes in and breathes out air.
quote: for nothing is internally viviparous unless it receive and breathe out air.
scope: Internally viviparous animals (man, viviparous quadrupeds, cetaceans)

label: Animals with lungs are hotter than animals without
claim: Animals with a lung are generally hotter than those without, and among them those whose lung is soft and full of blood are hottest.
quote: for generally those animals which have a lung are hotter than those which have not
scope: Air-breathing animals compared with gill-breathers and others

label: Heat and dryness explain why birds and reptiles lay complete eggs
claim: Birds and scaly reptiles lay a complete egg because they are hot, but only an egg rather than live young because they are dry; the reproductive mode follows from an animal's heat and moisture.
quote: For birds and scaly reptiles because of their heat produce a perfect egg, but because of their dryness it is only an egg
scope: Birds and scaly reptiles, within his heat-and-moisture account of viviparity and oviparity

label: All insects produce a scolex and all insects are bloodless
claim: All insects produce a scolex (larva), all insects are bloodless, and so every animal that produces a scolex is bloodless.
quote: All insects produce a scolex. Now all the insects are bloodless, wherefore all creatures that produce a scolex from themselves are so.

label: Nature orders generation in a graded series by heat and perfection
claim: Nature orders generation in a regular gradation: the hottest and most perfect animals bear live young internally, then come those viviparous after internal eggs, then those laying perfect eggs, then those laying imperfect eggs, and coldest of all those producing a scolex.
quote: We must observe how rightly Nature orders generation in regular gradation. The more perfect and hotter animals produce their young perfect in respect of quality
scope: All animals, from mammals to insects

label: Embryonic parts form in succession, not all together
claim: The parts of an embryo do not all exist from the start; some are visible in the embryo while others are not yet formed, so they come into being in succession.
quote: That the former is not the fact is plain even to the senses, for some of the parts are clearly visible as already existing in the embryo while others are not

label: The lung appears later than the heart in development though larger
claim: In development the lung appears later than the heart, even though it is larger, so late appearance is not due to small size.
quote: for the lung is of greater size than the heart, and yet appears later than the heart in the original development.

label: Semen is thick and white when emitted and becomes watery on cooling
claim: Semen is thick and white when it issues from the body but on cooling becomes liquid and colourless like water, and in frost it liquefies rather than freezing.
quote: For whereas when it issues from the animal it is thick and white, yet on cooling it becomes liquid as water, and its colour is that of water.

label: Semen is always white, including that of Ethiopians
claim: Semen is invariably white, so Herodotus was wrong that the semen of Ethiopians is black.
quote: for it is also an invariable rule that it is white, and Herodotus does not report the truth when he says that the semen of the Aethiopians is black
scope: Humans of all populations, and animals generally

label: General animal characters develop before those of the species
claim: An embryo does not become an animal and a particular kind of animal at the same time; the characters peculiar to the species develop last.
quote: For e.g. an animal does not become at the same time an animal and a man or a horse or any other particular animal. For the end is developed last, and the peculiar character of the species is the end of the generation in each individual.

label: Reason alone enters from outside and is divine
claim: Of the kinds of soul, reason alone enters the embryo from outside and alone is divine, since its activity has no connection with any bodily activity.
quote: It remains, then, for the reason alone so to enter and alone to be divine, for no bodily activity has any connexion with the activity of reason.

label: Some cartilaginous fishes complete development by connection to the uterus
claim: In some cartilaginous fishes, once the nutriment of the egg is used up, the embryo completes its development by connection with the uterus, so the egg is not released from the uterus.
quote: in other cases, when the nutriment from the egg is consumed, development is completed by connection with the uterus, and therefore the egg is not set free from the uterus.
scope: Selachians (cartilaginous fishes), e.g. placental sharks such as the smooth dogfish

label: Menstruation tends to come during the waning of the moon
claim: The menstrual period in women is not exactly fixed but tends to come during the waning of the moon, because bodies are colder when the environment is colder.
quote: The period is not accurately defined in women, but tends to return during the waning of the moon.

label: Hybrids come to resemble the female line over successive generations
claim: When different kinds are crossed, the first cross resembles both parents, but over successive generations the offspring come to resemble the female in form.
quote: the first cross has a common resemblance to both parents, as the hybrid between fox and dog, partridge and domestic fowl, but as time goes on and one generation springs from another, the final result resembles the female in form
scope: Crosses between related kinds (fox and dog, partridge and fowl), possible when gestation, breeding season and size are similar

label: The heart is the first part to be distinctly formed in all animals with blood
claim: In all animals with blood the heart is the first part to appear distinctly formed in the embryo, being the origin of the blood-vessels and of the other parts.
quote: Therefore it is that the heart appears first distinctly marked off in all the sanguinea
scope: Animals with blood (roughly vertebrates); the heart's analogue in bloodless animals

label: No male of the erythrinus has ever been seen
claim: No male of the fish called erythrinus has ever been seen, only females and specimens full of roe, which suggests it may generate without a male.
quote: No male of the so-called erythrinus has ever yet been seen, but females, and specimens full of roe, have been seen.
scope: The erythrinus (a Mediterranean fish, probably a sea bass or sea bream of the Serranidae or Sparidae)

label: Eels and some mullets are neither male nor female
claim: Some fishes are neither male nor female, such as eels and a kind of mullet found in stagnant waters.
quote: Again, some members of the class of fishes are neither male nor female, as eels and a kind of mullets found in stagnant waters.
scope: Eels (Anguilla) and a mullet of stagnant waters

label: Nature makes nothing in vain, so the male is needed for full generation
claim: Where the sexes are separate the female cannot generate perfectly alone, for otherwise the male would exist in vain, and Nature makes nothing in vain.
quote: But whenever the sexes are separate the female cannot generate perfectly by herself alone, for then the male would exist in vain, and Nature makes nothing in vain.

label: Internal parts form before external parts in the embryo
claim: In the embryo the internal parts come into being before the external, and the larger become visible before the smaller.
quote: After this, as said already, the internal parts come into being before the external.

label: Polydactylous quadrupeds bear blind young whose eyelids open after birth
claim: All polydactylous (many-toed) quadrupeds, such as the dog, lion, wolf, fox and jackal, bear their young blind, and the eyelids do not separate until after birth.
quote: Moreover, all polydactylous quadrupeds, as dog, lion, wolf, fox, jackal, produce their young blind, and the eyelids do not separate till after birth.
scope: Polydactylous (many-toed) quadrupeds: carnivores such as dog, lion, wolf, fox, jackal

label: In the early embryo the head and eyes are largest and the legs small
claim: In the embryo at an early stage the parts about the head, especially the eyes, appear largest and the parts below the navel, such as the legs, are small, because the lower parts exist for the sake of the upper.
quote: This is why the parts about the head, and particularly the eyes, appear largest in the embryo at an early stage, while the parts below the umbilicus, as the legs, are small
scope: Animal embryos with an upper and lower body

label: Eyes appear very large early but are the last parts to be completed
claim: The eyes of all animals, whether walking, swimming or flying, appear very large from the beginning of development but are the last parts to be completely formed, collapsing in the interval.
quote: Though from the beginning they appear very large in all creatures, whether they walk or swim or fly, yet they are the last of the parts to be formed completely, for in the intervening time they collapse.

label: The bregma is the last bone to form and is still soft after birth
claim: The bregma (the top of the skull) is the last bone to be formed and is still soft in children after birth, more so in man than in other animals because man's brain is the most fluid and largest.
quote: For this reason the ‘bregma’ is the last of the bones to be formed; even after birth this bone is still soft in children.
scope: Humans, compared with other animals with a brain

label: Bones set the limit of an animal's size
claim: Bones grow only up to a certain point, and they set the limit of size in animals; if bones could always grow, every animal with bone or its analogue would grow as long as it lived.
quote: if these had been always able to grow, all animals that have bone or its analogue would grow as long as they lived, for these set the limit of size to animals.
scope: Animals with bone or its analogue

label: Hair goes on growing after death
claim: Hair continues to grow after death, though it does not begin growing then.
quote: Hair actually goes on growing after death; it does not, however, begin growing then.

label: Of all bones only the teeth grow throughout life
claim: Of all the bones, the teeth alone go on growing throughout life, as shown by teeth that grow out of line until they no longer meet.
quote: Of all the bones they alone go on growing through life, as is plain with the teeth which grow out of the straight line so as no longer to touch each other.

label: Other animals are born with teeth but man is born without
claim: Other animals are born with teeth or their analogue, because they are more perfect at birth than man, whereas man is normally born without teeth.
quote: Other animals are born in possession of teeth or their analogue (unless in cases contrary to Nature), because when they are set free from the parent they are more perfect than man; but man (also unless in cases contrary to Nature) is born without them.
scope: Humans compared with other toothed animals

label: Man is the most naked animal and has the smallest nails for his size
claim: Man is the most naked of all animals and has the smallest nails in proportion to his size, because he has the least earthy residue.
quote: man is the most naked in body of all animals and has the smallest nails in proportion to his size

label: Umbilical cord vessel number rises with animal size
claim: The umbilical cord consists of blood-vessels in a sheath: more numerous in larger animals such as cattle, one in the smallest animals, and two in those of intermediate size.
quote: The cord consists of blood-vessels in a sheath, more numerous in the larger animals as cattle and the like, one in the smallest, two in those of intermediate size.
scope: Viviparous animals with an umbilical cord (placental mammals)

label: Animals lacking upper front teeth have cotyledons in the uterus
claim: All animals without front teeth in the upper jaw, and those with front teeth in both jaws whose uterus has many close blood-vessels rather than one great one, have cotyledons in the uterus; most with front teeth in both jaws and no horns lack them.
quote: All animals with no front teeth in the upper jaw, and all those which have them in both jaws and whose uterus has not one great blood-vessel running through it but many close together insteadall these have in the uterus the so-called cotyledons
scope: Viviparous quadrupeds; animals without upper incisors (ruminants) versus those with incisors in both jaws

label: Cotyledons shrink and disappear as the embryo matures
claim: As the embryo grows and approaches completion, the cotyledons in the uterus become smaller and finally disappear when it is fully formed.
quote: As the embryo grows and approaches perfection the cotyledons become smaller and finally disappear when it is perfected.
scope: Animals with cotyledons in the uterus (ruminants)

label: Of all hybrids only mules are sterile
claim: Animals born of crosses between different kinds can all mate and produce young of both sexes, except mules, which alone are sterile.
quote: Of the animals that arise from such union all except mules are found to copulate again with each other and to be able to produce young of both sexes, but mules alone are sterile
scope: Hybrids between related kinds (dogs, foxes, wolves, partridges and hens, hawks, rays), contrasted with mules

label: General theories not based on the special principles of a subject are empty
claim: All theories not based on the special principles of the subject in question are empty: in natural science one must reason from the facts peculiar to the kinds concerned, as geometry reasons from geometrical principles.
quote: For all theories not based on the special principles involved are empty; they only appear to be connected with the facts without being so really.

label: The ass cannot bear cold and is not found in cold regions
claim: The ass is of a cold nature and cannot bear cold, so it is not produced in wintry regions such as Scythia and the land of the Celts beyond Iberia.
quote: Again the ass is an animal of cold nature, and so is not wont to be produced in wintry regions because it cannot bear cold, as in Scythia and the neighbouring country and among the Celts beyond Iberia

label: The gestation period of both horse and ass is one year
claim: The period of gestation in both the horse and the ass is one year, so the mother gives birth in the same season as she was impregnated.
quote: for the mothers bear at the same season as that in which they are impregnated, the period of gestation in both horse and ass being one year.

label: The mule is sterile because the ass's cold seed chills the horse's
claim: Mules are sterile because the horse already tends to sterility and becomes wholly so when its generative secretion is chilled by mixing with the cold secretion of the ass.
quote: The horse is much the same; it tends naturally towards sterility, and to make it entirely so it is only necessary that its generative secretion should become colder; now this is what happens to it when mixed with the corresponding secretion of the ass.

label: A female mule can conceive but cannot carry the foal to birth
claim: A female mule can sometimes conceive, but she cannot nourish the embryo to birth because she has no menstrual secretion.
quote: Hence it is sometimes possible for the female to conceive, as has been known to happen before now, but it is impossible for her to complete the process of nourishing the embryo and bringing it to birth.

label: Selachians are internally oviparous but bring forth live young
claim: The cartilaginous fishes form an egg inside the uterus but give birth to live young; their egg is soft-shelled and of one colour.
quote: The cartilaginous fishes, as has been often said already, are oviparous internally but produce the young alive, the egg changing previously from one part of the uterus to another; and their egg is soft-shelled and of one colour.

label: Wind-eggs occur in heavy, prolific birds, not in birds of prey
claim: Unfertilised 'wind-eggs' are produced by birds that are not strong fliers or predators and that produce many young, not by birds of prey.
quote: Some embryos are formed in birds spontaneously, which are called wind-eggs and ‘zephyria’ by some; these occur in birds which are not given to flight nor rapine but which produce many young
scope: birds: fowls, partridges, pigeons contrasted with birds of prey

label: Birds of prey lay few eggs because residual matter goes to wings
claim: Because both wings and semen are made from the same residual matter, birds whose residue goes into wings and feathers (birds of prey) mate little and lay few eggs.
quote: Since then both the wings and the semen are made from residual matter, nature cannot afford to spend much upon both. And for this same reason the birds of prey are neither given to treading much nor to laying many eggs
scope: birds, especially birds of prey versus heavy ground birds

label: The cuckoo lays few eggs and lays them in other birds' nests
claim: The cuckoo, though not a bird of prey, lays few eggs, and it lays them in the nests of other birds; Aristotle attributes this to its cold, cowardly nature.
quote: The cuckoo, though not a bird of prey, lays few eggs, because it is of a cold nature, as is shown by the cowardice of the bird, whereas a generative animal should be hot and moist. That it is cowardly is plain, for it is pursued by all the birds and lays eggs in the nests of others.

label: The lioness bears five or six cubs, then fewer each year, then none
claim: A lioness produces five or six cubs at her first birth, four the next year, then three, and so down to one and finally none, as her generative secretion is used up with age.
quote: A similar condition is the cause of the later sterility of the lioness, for at the first birth she produces five or six, then in the next year four, and again three cubs, then the next number down to one, then none at all

label: Wind-eggs arise without any prior impregnation
claim: Unfertilised wind-eggs are not relics of a previous mating: they arise in hens and geese that have never been impregnated.
quote: Hence some are wont to speak of wind-eggs as not coming into being independently but as mere relics from a previous impregnation. But this is a false view, for sufficient observations have been made of their arising without impregnation in chickens and goslings.

label: Fish lay incomplete eggs because they are too numerous to finish inside
claim: Birds lay their eggs complete, whereas externally spawning fish lay incomplete eggs that finish growing outside the mother, because fish produce too many eggs for all to be completed inside her.
quote: Among creatures that lay eggs externally birds produce their egg perfect, fish imperfect, but the eggs of the latter complete their growth outside as has been said before. The reason is that the fish kind is very fertile; now it is impossible for many eggs to reach completion within the mother and therefore they lay them outside.

label: Bird eggs are two-coloured, all fish eggs one-coloured
claim: The eggs of birds are two-coloured (white and yolk), while the eggs of all fishes are of one colour.
quote: While the eggs of birds are two-coloured, those of all fish are one-coloured.

label: Water birds' eggs have larger, paler yolks than land birds' eggs
claim: Lake (water) birds, being moister and colder than land birds, lay eggs whose yolk is larger and less yellow.
quote: This is what we find in lake birds, for they are of a moister nature and are colder than the land birds, so that the so-called ‘lecithus’ or yolk in the eggs of such birds is large and less yellow because the white is less separated off from it.
scope: aquatic (lake) birds such as ducks and geese versus land birds

label: A hen's egg is laid with the sharp end last
claim: The sharp end of a bird's egg, where it was attached to the uterus, comes out of the hen after the blunt end.
quote: And this is why the sharp end of the egg comes out of the hen later than the blunt end; for the part attached to the uterus comes out later, and the egg is attached at the point where is the said principle, and the principle is in the sharp end.

label: The eggshell is soft when laid and hardens by cooling
claim: A bird's eggshell is still soft when the egg is laid and hardens immediately afterwards by cooling as its moisture evaporates.
quote: it is not observed that the shell is at first only a soft membrane, and that it is only after the egg is perfected that it becomes hard and brittle; this is so nicely adjusted that it is still soft when it comes out (for otherwise it would cause pain in laying), but no sooner has it come out than it is fixed hard by cooling

label: Live-bearing selachians keep the young attached to the uterus by an umbilicus
claim: In some cartilaginous fishes the egg stays attached to the uterus, and when the young fish is complete it is still connected to the uterus by an umbilical cord after the yolk is used up, as in the smooth dogfish.
quote: in some of the cartilaginous fish the egg is not detached from the uterus, but is still connected with it as it comes downwards with a view to the production of the young alive; in these the young fish when perfected is still connected by the umbilicus to the uterus when the egg has been consumed.
scope: some selachians, notably the 'smooth hound' (Mustelus, smooth dogfish)

label: Fish are prolific because most of their eggs are destroyed
claim: Most fish eggs that are laid are destroyed before hatching, and fish produce great numbers of eggs to make up for this loss.
quote: even as it is most of those laid are destroyed before hatching. Hence the class of fish is prolific, for Nature makes up for the destruction by numbers.

label: All fish have separate sexes except the erythrinus and the channa
claim: In all fishes some individuals have milt organs and others a uterus, except two kinds, the erythrinus and the channa, which have no separate males.
quote: But, as it is, some of them have organs for milt and others have a uterus, and this distinction obtains in all except two, the erythrinus and the channa, some of them having the milt organs, others a uterus.
scope: fishes; erythrinus and channa are probably sea perches (Serranus)

label: Female fish do not conceive by swallowing milt
claim: Fish are not conceived by the female swallowing the male's milt, because the passage from the mouth leads to the intestine, not the uterus.
quote: as if fish were conceived by the mother’s swallowing the milt,— not considering that this is impossible. For the passage which enters by way of the mouth runs to the intestines, not to the uterus

label: The hyena has only one kind of genitals, not both sexes
claim: The hyena does not have both male and female genitals; each animal has one, but both sexes have a mark under the tail resembling the female genitals.
quote: This is untrue, for the hyena has been seen to have only one pudendum, there being no lack of opportunity for observation in some districts, but hyenas have under the tail a line like the pudendum of the female.

label: Eggs fertilised by one cock take on the nature of a later cock
claim: Eggs already impregnated by one cock change to the nature of a second cock that treads the hen later, provided this happens before the white separates from the yolk.
quote: In birds the wind-eggs become fertile, and those previously impregnated by one kind of cock change their nature to that of the later cock.

label: Insect larvae become motionless, egg-like stages before the adult emerges
claim: Insect larvae, after reaching full size, become a sort of egg: their outer husk hardens and they are motionless, as in bees, wasps and caterpillars.
quote: All these products that are of the nature of a scolex, after progressing and acquiring their full size, become a sort of egg, for the husk about them hardens and they are motionless during this period. This is plain in the scolex of bees and wasps and in caterpillars.
scope: insects with a larval ('scolex') stage: bees, wasps, butterflies and moths

label: Some insects arise spontaneously in wool and water
claim: Some insects come into being without copulation, spontaneously, in wool and similar materials and in water.
quote: Similar to this is also what happens with all other insects which come into being without copulation in wool and other such materials and in water.
scope: insects such as clothes moths and aquatic insect larvae

label: Worker bees generate drones without copulation
claim: Worker bees produce drones without copulation, being female in generative power but containing both sexes as plants do.
quote: It remains then, as appears to be the case in certain fishes, that the bees should generate the drones without copulation, being indeed female in respect of generative power, but containing in themselves both sexes as plants do.

label: Bee kings generate both kings and workers
claim: The 'kings' (leaders) of a hive generate both their own kind and the worker bees.
quote: since those occupied with the tendance of these creatures deny this, it remains that the kings must generate both their own kind and the bees.
scope: the honey bee (Apis mellifera); 'kings' are queens

label: Fine seasons bring many drones, rainy seasons many workers
claim: In fine weather bees collect much honey and produce many drones, while in rainy seasons they produce a large brood of ordinary worker bees.
quote: Another fact is also natural, that in fine seasons much honey is collected and many drones are produced but in rainy reasons a large brood of ordinary bees.

label: Observation must take precedence over theory
claim: Where the facts are sufficiently known, credit should be given to observation rather than to theories, and to theories only if they agree with the observed facts.
quote: the facts, however, have not yet been sufficiently grasped; if ever they are, then credit must be given rather to observation than to theories, and to theories only if what they affirm agrees with the observed facts.

label: Few testaceans live on land, many in the sea
claim: Few or no kinds of testaceans (shelled molluscs and the like) live on land, snails being the exception, whereas in the sea there are many of every form.
quote: Because their nature answers to that of plants, therefore few or no kinds of testacea come into being on land, e.g. the snails and any others, few as they are, that resemble them; but in the sea and similar waters there are many of all kinds of forms.

label: Bloodless aquatic animals are rare in fresh water, common in estuaries
claim: Bloodless animals such as testaceans, cephalopods and crustaceans are not found in lakes or in the fresher brackish waters, except exceptionally, but arise in estuaries and at river mouths.
quote: Wherefore animals having no blood and not of a hot nature are not produced in lakes nor in the fresher among brackish waters, but only exceptionally, but it is in estuaries and at the mouths of rivers that they come into being, as testacea and cephalopoda and crustacea
scope: bloodless aquatic animals: testaceans, cephalopods, crustaceans

label: Eels and some river fishes arise from scolex-like 'entrails of earth'
claim: Some blooded animals, including a kind of mullet, some other river fishes and the eels, arise without parents in scolex form; eels come into being in the so-called 'entrails of earth'.
quote: even some sanguinea, as a kind of mullet and some other river fishes and also the eel kind. For all of these, though they have but little blood by nature, are nevertheless sanguinea, and have a heart with blood in it as the origin of the parts; and the so-called ‘entrails of earth’, in which comes into being the body of the eel, have the nature of a scolex.
scope: eels (Anguilla), a kind of mullet and some river fishes

label: All testaceans arise spontaneously from putrefying mud
claim: All testaceans are formed spontaneously, for example on the sides of boats when frothy mud putrefies.
quote: That all the testacea are formed spontaneously is clear from such facts as these. They come into being on the side of boats when the frothy mud putrefies.
scope: testaceans (shelled molluscs, barnacles and the like)

label: Male and female twins often lie in the same part of the uterus
claim: Male and female twins are often found together in the same part of the uterus, in all viviparous animals, land animals and fish alike.
quote: Moreover male and female twins are often found together in the same part of the uterus; this we have observed sufficiently by dissection in all the vivipara, both land animals and fish.

label: Fish and serpents have no testes yet produce both sexes
claim: Fishes and serpents have no testes, yet they produce both male and female offspring, so the testes do not determine sex.
quote: a proof of this is that many animals in which the distinction of sex exists, and which produce both male and female offspring, nevertheless have no testes, as the footless animals; I mean the classes of fish and of serpents.

label: The male is what can concoct blood into form-bearing semen
claim: The male is defined as the sex able to concoct blood into semen that carries the principle of form; the female receives semen but cannot form or emit it.
quote: For the male is that which can concoct the blood into semen and which can form and secrete and discharge a semen carrying with it the principle of form

label: Males are hotter than females
claim: Since concoction works by heat and the male concocts semen, the males of animals must be hotter than the females.
quote: And (2) all concoction works by means of heat. Therefore the males of animals must needs be hotter than the females.
scope: animals with separate sexes, especially those with blood

label: An embryo becomes female when the male principle fails for lack of heat
claim: An embryo becomes female when the male principle, through lack of heat, fails to master and concoct the material, which then changes into its opposite.
quote: For when the first principle does not bear sway and cannot concoct the nourishment through lack of heat nor bring it into its proper form, but is defeated in this respect, then must needs the material which it works on change into its opposite. Now the female is opposite to the male

label: Young and ageing parents produce more females
claim: Parents who are young or approaching old age produce more female offspring than those in their prime.
quote: For more females are produced by the young and by those verging on old age than by those in the prime of life; in the former the vital heat is not yet perfect, in the latter it is failing.

label: More males are conceived under north winds than south winds
claim: More males are born when copulation takes place while north winds blow than while south winds blow.
quote: Again, more males are born if copulation takes place when north than when south winds are blowing.

label: Menstruation naturally occurs when the moon is waning
claim: Menstruation naturally occurs more when the month (moon) is waning, that time being colder and moister.
quote: Also the fact that the catamenia occur in the course of nature rather when the month is waning is due to the same causes.

label: Offspring resemble parents more than remoter ancestors
claim: Children resemble their parents more than their remoter ancestors, and those ancestors more than any chance individual.
quote: (2) They resemble their parents more than remoter ancestors, and resemble those ancestors more than any chance individual.

label: Unmastered paternal movements revert to those of the grandfather
claim: When the movement from the father in the semen is weakened ('resolved'), it changes into that of his father and then his grandfather, and likewise in the maternal line, so that children may resemble grandparents and remoter ancestors.
quote: for instance, if the movement of the male parent be resolved, it changes by a very slight difference into that of his father, and in the next instance into that of his grandfather; and in this way not only in the male but also in the female line the movement of the female parent changes into that of her mother

label: Monstrosities are commonest in animals bearing many young, above all fowl
claim: Monstrosities are very rare in animals that bear one young, more frequent in those bearing many, and most frequent in birds, above all the domestic fowl.
quote: Hence also such monstrosities appear very rarely in animals producing only one young one, more frequently in those producing many, most of all in birds and among birds in the common fowl.
scope: animals generally; domestic fowl; humans compared with multiparous mammals
